findings.title: Chunked transfer-encoding chunk footer (CRLF) is discarded without validation, enabling request smuggling
findings.evidence:
In ChunkedReader.__call__, after a chunk's data is fully read, line 197 sets self._bytes_to_discard = 2. On the next call the two attacker-controlled bytes following the chunk are extracted at line 164 (buf.maybe_extract_at_most) and unconditionally consumed at line 167 (self._bytes_to_discard -= len(data)) with no comparison against b"
". Any two bytes are therefore accepted as the chunk terminator. Because a chunk boundary is determined by this unchecked count rather than by the literal CRLF, h11 can disagree with other HTTP processors about where a chunk ends. Confirmed by sending b"3
xxx__1a
": the stock 0.14.0 reader returns Data(data=b'xxx') and then waits for a 0x1a (26)-byte chunk, i.e. it treats the bytes after 'xxx' as a valid footer and reinterprets '1a' as the next chunk size, whereas a parser that scans for CRLF would treat 'xxx__1a' as the chunk body. This divergence is reachable by any remote peer that controls a chunked body (client to an h11 server, or upstream server to an h11 client) and is the classic precondition for HTTP request/response smuggling when h11 is deployed behind a proxy/load balancer (CWE-444). Upstream h11 0.16.0 fixed exactly this by storing the expected terminator b"
" and raising LocalProtocolError when the extracted bytes do not match (GHSA-vqfr-h8mv-ghfj / CVE-2025-43859: 'Reject certain malformed Transfer-Encoding: chunked bodies ... could have enabled request-smuggling attacks'). Note: this is the concrete root cause in the target; the trailer itself (lines 158-162) does call _decode_header_lines and is not the unchecked path.
